summary: Eq.(34) Fourier-Bessel closed form reproduces under independent implementation (C1). Fig.1-like transients at r=0.5 are broadly consistent in scale (~0.19-0.2) but depend on an apparent mismatch in stated initial condition and show alpha-ordering/shape discrepancies versus the paper narrative (C2). Conformable vs GL/Caputo agreement is good at alpha=1 but shows nontrivial differences for alpha<1 (up to ~16% rel L2 at alpha=0.5), so the claimed close match is only partially supported (C3). Fig.3a/3b 3D surfaces were not quantitatively replicated here beyond plausibility/consistency checks (C4-C5).

notes.c1_basis: Independent NumPy Fourier-Bessel evaluation of Eq.(34) with N=60 modes reproduces the conformable solution behavior; no internal inconsistencies detected in the closed-form implementation for the stated R=1, f=1, beta=1 setup.
notes.c2_basis: At r=0.5, u_max ~0.187-0.188 (consistent with y-max ~0.2). However: (i) Fig.1 shape matches u0=0 rather than the paper text u0=sin(pi r); (ii) alpha-ordering from Eq.(34) reproduction is opposite to the paper description; (iii) transient timing differs strongly with alpha (t_half increases with alpha).
notes.c3_basis: Conformable vs GL metrics at r=0.5: alpha=1 matches tightly (max_abs_diff ~1e-4, rel_L2 ~3.6e-4), but alpha=0.75 shows moderate mismatch (rel_L2 ~0.105), alpha=0.5 larger mismatch (rel_L2 ~0.164, max_abs_diff ~0.055). This does not support a general 'matches GL numerical Caputo-fractional solution' claim except near alpha=1.
notes.c4_basis: Only spot-checked qualitatively (no digitized surface/quantitative comparison).
notes.c5_basis: Only spot-checked qualitatively (no digitized surface/quantitative comparison).
global_caveats: beta not stated in the paper; chose beta=1 for classical steady-state consistency with Fig 1 y-scale.
Paper's textual description of Fig 1 initial condition is inconsistent with what the plotted curves show.
Conformable derivative math per Eq (34) is faithfully reproduced; the qualitative alpha-ordering discrepancy is a paper narrative issue, not a replication error.
